meta.title: Potential hotspots
meta.note: Public planning frames only. Pick one shock so the family table stays honest. Not a forecast, not a targeting list, not a war plan.

hotspots.label: Taiwan Strait
hotspots.why: Most-discussed high-end shock: chips, shipping, fuel, and rumor hit a U.S. house even if no bomb falls here.
hotspots.doNot: Do not name real bases, cables, or plants as targets. Talk prices, delays, and family decisions.
hotspots.mission: Keep this family functioning while a Taiwan Strait crisis shocks shipping, energy, electronics, and trust. You cannot command fleets. You can keep water, medicine, and a check-in.

theater.H-01: Taiwan Strait: open-source and official U.S. statements disagree on whether PLA activity is coercion, an exercise, or open conflict.
theater.H-02: Japan, the Philippines, or insurers limit transit and raise rates on Taiwan-adjacent shipping. Chip and energy cargoes slip.
theater.H-03: Cable congestion, cyber noise, and overloaded U.S. networks make official guidance late. Some channels still work.
theater.H-04: Taiwan and nearby ports face civilian movement. U.S. clinics and pharmacies begin to slow.
theater.H-05: U.S. and partner magazine depth, tankers, and industrial surge look oversold. Tempo cannot be kept.
theater.H-06: A viral video of a contested incident near Taiwan contradicts official U.S. and PRC accounts.

hotspots.label: Canada / northern trade
hotspots.why: Not a likely shooting war with Ottawa. It is a likely way a U.S. house gets cold, dark, or expensive: electricity ties, oil and gas, auto parts, winter roads, and a rumor mill about the northern border.
hitsHome: Power and heating fuel in northern-tier states
Winter isolation if roads and rail snarl
hotspots.doNot: Canada is a neighbor, not a target set. Do not name dams, pipelines, or border crossings as things to attack. Talk outages, prices, and who you call.
hotspots.mission: Keep this family functioning if U.S.–Canada trade, power, or fuel gets ugly. You cannot run NORAD. You can keep heat, water, medicine, and a neighbor check-in through a northern winter week.

theater.H-01: Officials in Washington and Ottawa disagree on whether a northern crisis is a labor/energy dispute, a cyber event, or something worse. Markets move first.
theater.H-02: Cross-border freight and some electricity or fuel flows tighten. Insurers and trucking delay. Relatives in another state want a warm room.
theater.H-03: Phones and data get ugly in a cold snap while agencies argue. Weather radio and a landline-style backup still matter.
theater.H-04: Clinics slow; a pharmacy is short; heating and medical devices compete for power. Canada and U.S. systems both feel the strain.
theater.H-05: Pay, fuel, and restock lag. Card readers flake. A grocer is light on staples that usually roll north–south.
theater.H-06: A viral clip of a border or grid incident splits the family group. Rent, heat, and work paperwork still come due.

hotspots.label: Mexico / southern trade
hotspots.why: Not a plan to fight Mexico. It is a likely way a U.S. house feels a shock: produce, auto parts, energy, Gulf shipping, and delayed border freight — plus rumor about the southern line.
hitsHome: Food prices and empty produce shelves
Auto and factory layoffs or delays
Fuel on the Gulf and southern tier
hotspots.doNot: Mexico is a neighbor, not a target set. Do not name ports, bridges, or pipelines as things to attack. Talk food, fuel, work, and family movement.
hotspots.mission: Keep this family functioning if U.S.–Mexico trade, fuel, or food logistics get ugly. You cannot control a border. You can keep water, food, medicine, and a sharing rule that does not wreck the household.

theater.H-01: Washington and Mexico City disagree on whether violence, a port halt, or an energy event is a local crisis or a wider shock. Stores are still open.
theater.H-02: Southern freight and some fuel tighten. Produce and parts run late. A relative wants a ride or a spare room farther north.
theater.H-03: Phones and data congest along the southern tier. Official guidance is late. A weather radio or second method still works.
theater.H-04: Pharmacies and clinics slow as restock from cross-border supply wobbles. Heat makes medical delay worse.
theater.H-05: Pay, fuel, and groceries lag. Cash works; some cards do not. Sharing without a floor bankrupts the givers.
theater.H-06: A viral border video contradicts official accounts. Arguments get bitter. Insurance, rent, and work still matter.
